title: Etale criterion for geometric connectedness of a fibre
statement: Let $g:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $s\in S$. The scheme-theoretic fibre $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is geometrically connected [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] if and only if, for every etale neighbourhood $(U,u)\to(S,s)$, the base-changed fibre $X_u=X\times_SU\times_U\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme].

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 37.53.6 (Tag 03GZ, label lemma-characterize-geometrically-connected-fibres, line 15219)

proof.text: Use Mathlib isPullback_fiberToSpecResidueField_of_isPullback on the canonical pullback square for g and the neighbourhood map e. After replacing s by e(t), this gives the neighbourhood fibre as a cartesian square over the fibre g.fiber s and Spec κ(t). Geometric connectedness applies to this square directly, without a finite-separability hypothesis on the residue extension.

source.place: Tag 03GZ, proof, forward implication; cartesian identification by Mathlib fibre pullback lemma

proof.text: For the converse apply the finite-separable test to g.fiber s with its canonical structure morphism. For each finite separable extension K/κ(s), realize K as the residue field of an etale neighbourhood by the prescribed-residue-field theorem, with its compatible field isomorphism.

Apply Spec to the compatible residue-field isomorphism. Spec.map_comp and ring-map extensionality show that it identifies the residue-field map with the algebra map into K. Transport the cartesian square of the first step using IsPullback.of_iso, leaving its top-left corner unchanged. Its isoPullback induces a homeomorphism to the tested field base change. Transfer the assumed ConnectedSpace instance along that homeomorphism; the finite-separable criterion then proves geometric connectedness.
